messages:
maya: Quick thread 7: we need to resolve the triage tension: do we prioritize the enterprise customer's feature request (high strategic value but ~8 dev days) or clear the three mid-sev bugs clogging search for a large user cohort? Need deterministic rule so we can publish commitments.

ajay: i'd bias to fixes if they materially affect daily flows. feature can be scheduled next cycle unless it's contractually promised.

courtney: can we quantify expected impact? feature = 2 enterprise logos closing + long-term eng velocity gain, but takes ~1.5 sprint. Bugs = ~3% DAU struggling with search ranking, affects retention signal.

ben: From SRE/data: search bug increases p75 latency by ~30ms and misranks ~0.8% of requests. Retention delta unknown but measurable over 2 weeks.

sara: operational risk: one of the bugs touches the migration path. Quick fix might require DB rollout checks. That could blow timeline unless we spike.

oliver: proposal: apply a decision matrix: strategic-adjacent requests with >1 enterprise ARR impact go to expedited planning; otherwise prioritize user-impacted regressions. Also we should reserve a single "strategic buffer" sprint slot (max 20% capacity) for emergent enterprise work.

maya: concrete ops: two tracks. Track A (urgent): P0-P1 regressions with measurable user impact -> hotpatch/next sprint priority. Track B (strategic): enterprise asks that pass a 3-criterion gate: 1) documented ARR influence 2) clear acceptance metric 3) plan for <=8 dev-days or broken into a 3-day spike + follow-on. If Track B passes, move into buffer.

courtney: can we write the gate as a checklist on the ticket? I'll add fields: "ARR-case", "metric to move needle", "breakdown plan". If missing, default to Track A.

dena: from customer success: two customers will consider expansion if the enterprise feature ships in Q3. We should give them a realistic ETA if we accept.

ajay: operational ask: if we take the feature into buffer, don't let it block the urgent bug fixes. Dev leads must protect the hotfix lane.

lydia: i'll run a quick spike to break the feature into smaller deliverables and estimate. 2-day spike OK?

maya: yes please. Lydia do the spike, add ARR-case and acceptance metric fields to ticket by EOD. Owners: bugs -> ajay + ben (next sprint), feature spike -> lydia, product comms -> dena.

sara: i'll draft the DB rollout checklist template for the bug that touches migration and add smoke tests.

release-bot: FYI: scheduled maintenance window available Thu 07:00-08:30 UTC. Label any canary PRs `patch/canary`.

maya: thanks everyone. We'll re-check Fri after spike and updated backlog fields. If spike shows feature breaks into <4d chunks we can push one chunk into the buffer this cycle. Otherwise feature goes to next planning cycle. :white_check_mark:
